briefs.explicit:
MISSION BRIEF S-004
Units: metres, seconds, kilograms. Time starts at t = 0 when every robot leaves its start location.

Locations (x, y, zone):
- base: (0, 0), outdoor
- north roof: (85, -106), roof
- control room: (-17, -28), indoor
- east fence: (-58, -69), outdoor
- fuel depot: (-115, -23), outdoor

Robots:
- M1 (mobile_manipulator): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 1.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 5 kg), robotic arm, camera. Endurance: 3300 s, including the return to its start.
- D1 (quadcopter): starts at base. Flies in straight lines at 8 m/s; can reach outdoor and roof locations, not indoor ones. Equipment: camera, cargo carrier (max 2 kg), thermal camera. Endurance: 1140 s, including the return to its start.
- G1 (rover): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 1.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 28 kg), camera, thermal camera. Endurance: 4920 s, including the return to its start.

Tasks:
- T1: Deliver the pressure gauge (6 kg) to fuel depot. Location: fuel depot. Duration: 60 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 6 kg). Deadline: finished by t = 300 s.
- T2: Deliver the spare pump (13 kg) to fuel depot. Location: fuel depot. Duration: 30 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 13 kg). Deadline: finished by t = 300 s.
- T3: Photograph east fence for the condition report. Location: east fence. Duration: 120 s. Needs: camera.
- T4: Replace the filter cartridge at control room. Location: control room. Duration: 180 s. Needs: robotic arm.
- T5: Inspect north roof with a camera. Location: north roof. Duration: 150 s. Needs: camera.

Rules:
1. Every task is done by exactly one robot. A robot does its tasks one at a time, in the order you list them, travelling between task locations.
2. A robot can only do a task if it has the needed equipment, enough payload capacity, and can reach the task location.
3. A task that must start after another task waits until that task is finished, even if a different robot does it.
4. Each robot must be back at its start location before its endurance runs out.
5. Every task must be finished by t = 600 s.

Objective: minimise the finish time of the last task (the makespan).
briefs.informal:
Here's what we need from the robots today.

Positions are in metres from the base at (0, 0). Drones fly straight and can't go indoors; ground robots follow the road grid (so they travel |dx| + |dy|) and can't get onto roofs. Everyone leaves their start spot at time zero.

Places: north roof (85, -106, a rooftop); control room (-17, -28, indoors); east fence (-58, -69, outside); fuel depot (-115, -23, outside).

The fleet: M1 is our mobile manipulator at base: gripper arm, camera, room for 5 kg, moves at 1.5 m/s and lasts 55 minutes including getting back. D1 is a quadcopter at base with a camera and a thermal camera; it flies at 8 m/s, can lift 2 kg, and its battery lasts 19 minutes including the flight home. G1 is a rover parked at base that hauls up to 28 kg at 1.5 m/s and runs for 82 minutes including the drive back. It has a camera and a thermal camera.

Jobs:
(T1) Drop the pressure gauge off at fuel depot; it weighs 6 kg - that takes 1 minute on site and it has to be finished within the first 5 minutes.
(T2) Drop the spare pump off at fuel depot; it weighs 13 kg - that takes 0.5 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 5 minutes.
(T3) We need pictures of east fence for the report - that takes 2 minutes on site.
(T4) Change the filter at control room - that takes 3 minutes on site.
(T5) Have a look at north roof - that takes 2.5 minutes on site.

Everything has to be wrapped up within 10 minutes of the start, and the sooner the last job finishes, the better. Every robot has to make it back to where it started before its battery runs out.
